{{Short description|45th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1975–76 National Hurling League |image = |dates =5 October 1975 – 20 June 1976 |teams = 20 |team1 = Kilkenny |captain1 = [[Phil Larkin]] |manager1 = |titles = 4th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |two= Wicklow |previous = [[1974–75 National Hurling League|1974–75]] |next = [[1976–77 National Hurling League|1976–77]] }} The '''1975–76 National Hurling League''' was the 45th season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1975-76 |winners=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]

(25 April 1976) |matches= 51 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1974-75 National Hurling League|1974-75]] |nextseason=[[1976-77 National Hurling League|1976-77]] |updated=28 February 2017 }} [[Galway GAA|Galway]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1974-75 National Hurling League|1974-75 season]]. [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 20 June 1976, [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] won the title after a 6–14 to 1–14 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final. It was their 4th league title overall and their first since [[1965-66 National Hurling League|1965-66]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} Westmeath were relegated from Division 1 after just one season in the top flight. They were defeated by [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] in a relegation play-off. Kilkenny's [[Eddie Keher]] was the Division 1 top scorer with 11–58. ===Structure=== The 14 teams in Division 1 were divided into two groups of seven teams named Division 1A and Division 1B. Each team played all the others in its group once. Two points were awarded for a win and one for a draw. The first two teams in Division 1A advanced to the league semi-finals. The third and fourth-placed teams in Division 1A joined the first two teams in Division 1B in the quarter-finals. The bottom-placed team in Division 1A was relegated to Division 1B with the Division 1B champion gaining promotion.
